question: How did Hunter Gimbel grow Gaber Group through partnership with other financial professionals like Howard Sharkman?
transcript_excerpt: Hunter Gimbel became strategic partners with Howard Sharkman through the Penn Mutual Star Study Group over the last four or five years. Although they work in completely different firms, they have worked together on numerous cases, providing value to clients across the continental US in private equity and banking, both for existing clients and referrals. This collaboration allowed Gimbel to deepen his bench without necessarily adding someone internally to the firm.

question: What is the Penn Mutual Star Study Group and how does it help financial professionals find collaboration partners?
transcript_excerpt: The Penn Mutual Star Study Group is a group of both career and independent financial network advisors and companies that are top in the life insurance business and do a significant amount of production with Penn Mutual as well as many other carriers. It provides the ability to meet other successful advisors and has helped Hunter Gimbel connect with strategic partners who operate in similar spaces and work well together across different organizations.

question: How does Gaber Group prepare clients before they meet with trust and estate attorneys to reduce legal fees?
transcript_excerpt: Gaber Group does internal design work and maps everything out so that by the time a client meets with a trust and estate lawyer, their entire estate diagram is filled out and completed. This makes the attorney's job easier and saves clients probably 20% to 30% of the estate planning fee, and cuts down the time from wanting to update estate planning to execution from six to twelve months to three to four months for most clients.

question: What advice does Hunter Gimbel give financial professionals starting to build partnerships for the first time?
transcript_excerpt: Gimbel recommends ensuring you have the same culture, beliefs, and are comfortable with the advisor. It is also helpful if they work inside the markets or with the types of clients you serve. He suggests reaching out to Penn Mutual's advanced planning team or your managing director to identify the right partner or partners, and notes that not all joint work partnerships will work—it may take trying different people and organizations to find the right fit.

question: How has Gaber Group's referral relationship with trust and estate law firms evolved into reciprocal business?
transcript_excerpt: Gaber Group introduces 50 to 60 clients a year to trust and estate law firms and provides significant value through the internal design work and preparation they complete beforehand. Because of this value and collaboration, those law firms now refer business back to Gaber Group when there are opportunities for insurance audits, sophisticated estate planning, buy-sell work, and succession planning, making Gaber Group one of their preferred firms.
